Working notes (through Day 10):
- Demand: 3, 7, 3, 4, 11, 2, 7, 2, 3. Average ~4.7/day, but volatile; spikes reach 7-11. Use 11 as the observed risk level.
- Costs: holding is cheap (~0.05/unit/day); fixed order cost 0.50; stockouts are very expensive. Day 6 stockout cost 11.00 and Day 8 cost 2.00. These dominate all holding/order costs.
- Critical failure: letting stock fall to 0-2 before demand spikes. Day 6 started with 2 and sold 11; Day 8 started with 2 and sold 7. Safety stock is necessary.
- Lead time: arrivals often occur 1-2 days later. Do not rely on same-day replenishment. Keep at least 2 days of cover, preferably 10+ units before reordering.
- Ordering: intermittent small orders cost 0.50 each and did not prevent stockouts. Order earlier and in larger batches to cover lead time and spikes.
- Counts: morning counts matched the system. Cycle count is scheduled for month end. New receiving temp observed; no errors yet.
- Action rule: monitor daily. If on-hand + incoming < 10, order enough to reach about 15 units, accounting for 1-2 day lead time. Do not wait for zero.
- With average demand ~5, 10 units covers 2 days; because stockout penalties are high, a larger buffer is justified.

Working notes (through Day 20):
- Demand is volatile. Last 14 days: 2,7,2,3,5,7,0,15,3,0,1,0,2,6. Recent average is lower (~3.8/day), but a spike reached 15. Use 15/day as the observed risk level, not 11.
- Costs: holding is cheap (~0.05/unit/day). Fixed order cost is 0.50, minor. Stockouts dominate: recent penalties include 9.00, 7.00, 5.50, 5.00, 3.50, etc. Prevent stockouts over minimizing holding/orders.
- Lead time: incoming is listed over the next 2 days. Orders can take up to 2 days. Do not assume same-day or next-day replenishment.
- Critical correction: the old rule “if on-hand + incoming < 10, order to 15” failed badly. It allowed repeated zero stock and sold-out days. Day 11’s 18-unit order still did not prevent a stockout.
- Action rule: monitor daily. Compute on-hand + scheduled arrivals over the next 2 days. If this cover is below 30, order enough to reach about 40. If stock is 0 or very low with no imminent arrival, order immediately. Do not wait for zero.
- Rationale: 15/day spike × 2-day lead time = 30 units needed before new orders arrive. Add buffer because stockouts cost far more than holding or ordering.
- Order timing: carrier pickup moved to 3pm; place orders before the cutoff.
- Counts: morning counts have matched the system. Cycle count is month-end. New receiving temp has no errors yet, but monitor receiving.
- Noise to ignore unless problems appear: racking rotation, pickup schedule changes, cycle-count reminders.

Working notes through Day 30:
- Demand: last 14 days: 1,0,2,6,4,7,9,10,4,6,6,9,6,5. Avg ~5.4/day, recent range 0–10; historical spike 15. Treat 10/day as current planning high, but keep buffer for possible 15.
- Costs: holding now dominates (0.10–2.00/day); ordering 0.50; no stockouts Days21–30. Stockouts remain very expensive, so avoid them.
- Lead time: incoming listed over next 2 days; orders can take up to 2 days. Do not assume same/next-day. Carrier pickup at 3pm; order before cutoff.
- Rule that worked: compute on-hand + next-2-day arrivals. If cover <30, order enough to reach ~40. If stock is 0/very low with no imminent arrival, order immediately. This produced zero stockouts for 10 days, though holding cost is high.
- Consideration: if demand stays ≤10/day and no stockouts, test lowering target modestly (e.g. 35) to cut holding, but only cautiously. Do not revert to old <10/order-to-15 rule; it failed.
- Counts: morning counts match. Cycle count at month-end. New receiving temp started Day23; no errors yet, monitor.
- Noise unless problem appears: racking rotation, pickup schedule note, forklift certification, cycle-count reminders.

Working notes through Day 40:

- Rule that works: compute on-hand + next-2-day arrivals. If cover <30, order enough to reach ~40. If stock is 0/very low with no imminent arrival, order immediately. This produced zero stockouts for 20 days, though holding cost is high.

Working notes through Day 50:
- Demand last 14 days: 14,5,4,6,11,8,8,4,2,5,7,8,3,8. Avg ~6.6/day; recent 9 days avg ~5.9, all ≤10; range 2–14; historical spike 15. Plan ~12/day with spike buffer, not 15 now.
- Costs: holding dominates (0.60–2.90/day recent); ordering 0.50; no stockouts Days21–50. Stockouts remain very expensive; avoid. Target ~40 now over-holds; lower.
- Lead time: arrivals listed over next 2 days; orders can take up to 2 days. Carrier pickup at 3pm; order before cutoff. Do not assume same/next-day.
- Revised rule: compute on-hand + next-2-day arrivals. Since demand moderated and 9+ days ≤10 with no stockouts, lower target from ~40 to ~30–32. If cover <24, order enough to reach ~32. If stock is 0/very low with no imminent arrival, order immediately. This should cut holding while keeping spike safety.
- Keep safety buffer: spikes to 14/15 still occur. Revisit target only if demand stays ≤10 and no stockouts continue.
- Counts: morning counts match; cycle count at month-end. Receiving temps: first started Day23, another Day45; no errors yet, monitor.

Working notes through Day 60:

- Costs: holding 0.30–2.20/day recent; ordering 0.50; Day56 stockout cost 6.00. Stockouts dominate; avoid.
- Lead time: arrivals listed next 2 days; orders may take up to 2 days. Carrier cutoff 3pm. Do not assume same/next-day.
- Revised target: raise from ~30–32 to ~34–36. Day56 showed 32-style cover too thin when first next-day arrival was 0 and demand spiked. Compute on-hand + next-2-day arrivals. If cover <24, order enough to reach ~34–36. Also check next-day arrival separately: if next-day arrival is 0 and on-hand ≤ expected next-day demand (~8–10), order immediately to cover gap. If stock 0/very low and no imminent arrival, order immediately.
- Keep spike safety: 14s still occur. Revisit target down only after no stockouts and demand ≤10 for multiple weeks.
- Counts: morning counts match; cycle count at month-end. Receiving temps started Day23, Day45, Day51, Day54, Day60; no errors yet, monitor.
- Noise unless problem appears: racking rotation, pickup schedule/cutoff, forklift certification, cycle-count reminders, ops notes.

Working notes through Day 70:
- Demand last 14: 5,8,8,4,6,3,12,12,4,14,6,12,8,10. Avg ~8.0/day; range 3–14; spikes 12–14 frequent. Demand is higher than prior ~6.9; do not lower target.
- Costs: holding 0.40–1.90/day; ordering 0.50; stockout Day69 2.00; Day56 6.00. Stockouts still dominate; avoid.
- Lead time: arrivals listed next 2 days; orders may take up to 2 days. Carrier cutoff 3pm. Same/next-day arrival not safe.
- Target: keep pipeline ~34–36 (on-hand + next-2 arrivals). If cover <34, order up to ~36. But Day69 showed zero-arrival gap: on-hand 10, next-day arrival 0, order 8 too late, stockout 2.00. So when a zero-arrival day is coming, on-hand entering it must be ≥14–16; order at least 2 days ahead. If next-day arrival is 0 and on-hand <16, order extra now; if already too late, raise buffer afterward.
- If stock 0/very low and no imminent arrival, order immediately. Day70 stock 0 with same-day arrival 18, order 0 was fine.
- Keep spike safety; revisit target down only after no stockouts and demand ≤10 for multiple weeks.
- Counts: morning counts matched; cycle count month-end. Receiving temps Day23,45,51,54,60,68; no errors yet, monitor.
- Noise unless problem: racking rotation, pickup schedule/cutoff, forklift certification, cycle-count reminders, ops notes.
